reason: This passage (Exodus 3) describes God hearing the cry of the Israelites, seeing their affliction under Egyptian oppression, and actively committing to liberate them. God identifies the Israelites as 'my people' (עַמִּ֥י) and sends Moses to bring them out of Egypt. The text demonstrates God's responsiveness to Israel's suffering and explicit commitment to their liberation. There is no indication whatsoever that God considers replacing Israel with another people, nor does the passage address whether Yahweh 'owes' loyalty. Instead, the passage shows God taking initiative to rescue the Israelites, demonstrating care and dedication toward them.
